sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in St. Clair Shores, Michigan?
sections.html:
Water shapes almost every sale in St. Clair Shores, from the lakefront and canal homes to the flood-zone questions that come up during financing. About 19 percent of the city's area is water, and a portion of it sits in the FEMA floodplain, so find out your flood status before you list.

St. Clair Shores is a Macomb County city on the western shore of Lake St. Clair, roughly 14 miles northeast of downtown Detroit. The Census Bureau puts its population at 57,872 for July 2025. Owners usually choose between three routes:

  • Listing with an agent, which suits a house in good condition and a seller who can wait for a buyer's financing.
  • Selling without an agent, which saves commission and puts the contract and the title steps on you.
  • Selling for cash as-is, which fits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant or an estate. Compare offers and read who pays which closing costs.

The sections below cover the local facts that affect each route.

sections.h2: What is St. Clair Shores like for a home seller?
sections.html:
The city covers 14.40 square miles in total, of which 2.72 square miles are water. Wikipedia reports about 14 miles of canals, most of them along the Nautical Mile, the stretch of Jefferson Avenue between 9 Mile and 10 Mile Roads with restaurants, boat dealers and marinas. The 28-story Shore Club Sky Tower at the foot of Nine Mile Road is the tallest structure in the city.

French settlers were in the area as early as 1710, and it stayed mostly farmland into the early twentieth century. It became a village in 1925 and a city in January 1951. Wikipedia describes St. Clair Shores as the fastest-growing suburb of Detroit during the 1950s, once subdivisions platted decades earlier finally filled in. The Jefferson Beach Amusement Park operated on the lakefront from 1927 until 1959.

Youth hockey is a local tradition, and the city runs two municipal indoor ice arenas at its civic recreation center. Interstate 94 runs along the western edge, with exits 224 through 230, and leads about 13 miles southwest to midtown Detroit.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about St. Clair Shores housing?
sections.html:
St. Clair Shores has the highest ownership rate and the highest household income of the four cities in the Census comparison table used for these pages.

sections.h2: How does the FEMA floodplain affect a St. Clair Shores sale?
sections.html:
A portion of the city lies inside the FEMA flood plain, and the city's own FEMA page says FEMA redraws the maps periodically, so a property that was inside the plain in earlier years may now be outside it, and the reverse can also happen. Insurers and lenders commonly look at the flood status of an address, so a buyer may ask about it.

To check yours, the city points to two tools:

  • Macomb County GIS: enter the address, open Layers, then Natural Features, and turn on Flood Zones. The parcel may be in the flood zone if it turns red.
  • FEMA's flood map search by street address.

If your insurer has placed the house in the floodplain but you hold a survey or other evidence that says otherwise, the city says you may qualify for a Letter of Map Amendment or can use the Options to Appeal Determination form. Sorting that out before you list avoids a surprise during the buyer's loan process.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads matter to St. Clair Shores buyers?
sections.html:
The city is split among three public school districts. South Lake Schools serves the southern part, Lakeview Public Schools the central part and Lake Shore Public Schools the northern part, and each district runs one high school inside the city. Buyers often ask which district a street belongs to, so confirm it for your address with the districts.

Private schools include St. Isaac Jogues and St. Joan of Arc; St. Germaine closed in 2024. Wikipedia notes that the city's popularity rests on its lakefront location, municipal park system, recreation programs and the choice of three districts.

For commuters, I-94 is the main artery, with Jefferson Avenue along the lake. The Census figure for mean travel time to work is 26.7 minutes, the longest among the four cities compared here.

sections.h2: What are the St. Clair Shores rules for rental houses?
sections.html:
A non-owner-occupied house in St. Clair Shores must be registered with the city, and a certificate of approval is required before anyone occupies it. The registration application prints these terms:

  • A single-family house costs $150 for the first 3,000 square feet, plus $10 for each additional 1,000 square feet.
  • A multiple-family building costs $150 for the first unit, plus $50 for each additional unit in the same building.
  • The fee covers the original inspection and one follow-up. A rescheduled inspection when no one is at the site costs $30, and a reinspection for non-compliance costs 50 percent of the original fee.
  • An owner outside Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Washtenaw and St. Clair counties must name a local agent.
  • If the property has been sold, the seller supplies a copy of the recorded deed or land contract to be removed from the city's records.

Call Community Development and Inspections at 586-447-3340 to confirm what applies to your address, and ask whether anything on file needs closing out before a sale, such as an open permit.

sections.h2: How do recording and transfer work in Macomb County?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded with the Macomb County Register of Deeds at 120 N. Main St. in Mount Clemens. The office lists a flat recording fee of $30 per document regardless of page count, and $4 of that goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund.

Warranty deeds, deeds with a warranty or covenant clause, land contracts and land contract assignments need a tax certificate from the County Treasurer before recording. The Register of Deeds page lists that certificate at $5 for up to five legal descriptions.

The county's transfer tax schedule prints the state rate as the sale price multiplied by 0.0075 and the county rate as the sale price multiplied by 0.0011. Ask your title company for the exact figure at your price. The Register of Deeds can be reached at (586) 469-7953.

After closing, Michigan Treasury guidance sets a 45-day window for the buyer to file the Property Transfer Affidavit, Form 2766, with the local assessor.

faqs.q: Is my St. Clair Shores house in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Check with Macomb County GIS or FEMA's flood map search, both of which the city links. A portion of the city is in the FEMA floodplain. If a survey shows otherwise, the city says you may qualify for a Letter of Map Amendment.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Macomb County?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds lists a flat $30 per document. The state transfer tax rate is the sale price times 0.0075 and the county rate is the sale price times 0.0011, according to the county's schedule.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house in St. Clair Shores?
faqs.a: Yes. A non-owner-occupied house must be registered and must hold a certificate of approval before anyone occupies it. A single-family house starts at $150 for the first 3,000 square feet.

faqs.q: Which school district is my St. Clair Shores house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the part of the city. South Lake Schools serves the southern portion, Lakeview Public Schools the central portion and Lake Shore Public Schools the northern portion. Verify the address with the district.

faqs.q: How big is St. Clair Shores?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists 11.68 square miles of land, and Wikipedia gives a total area of 14.40 square miles with 2.72 square miles of water. The city's population was 58,874 in the 2020 census.
